newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy will give temporary sanctuary to Albanians.
newsitem.headline: Italy will give temporary sanctuary to Albanians.

text.p: Italy said on Saturday that it would give temporary sanctuary to Albanians fleeing to its shores but intended to repatriate them once the armed anarchy in their country had subsided.

A senior government official, Nicola Sinisi, announced the policy after a two-hour meeting of police and immigration chiefs held in response to a recent influx of some 1,600 Albanians in a flotilla of creaking boats.

Sinisi, a junior interior minister, said refugees would not be considered for political asylum because the crisis in Albania was a "degeneration of public order" rather than a war. However, he confirmed they could stay in Italy temporarily.
"At this stage we have the duty for humanitarian reasons to keep people who are not able to live in their country. However, we have the duty to do this only for a limited period of time.
"At the end of this period, they will be repatriated. First on a voluntary basis and later through other means," Sinisi told reporters in the southeast Italian port of Brindisi.

He said boats that had arrived from Albania, many of them naval vessels, would be impounded so they could not be used for further crossings. He also said Italy was not facing a mass exodus of Albanians. "There is no crisis situation," he said.
